title: Voice Live and turn detection
summary: Voice Live is Azure's managed speech-to-speech service. Turn detection decides when a caller has finished and when to let them interrupt, and it is the setting that most changes how a voice agent feels.
useIf: You build a voice agent on Azure, or tune when an agent should start and stop talking.
avoidIf: You need a stage-by-stage pipeline you can inspect, or the whole stack must be GA only, in which case check each Voice Live surface first.

explain.md: **Voice Live** bundles speech recognition, a generative model and speech synthesis behind one WebSocket interface whose events mostly match the Azure OpenAI Realtime API [[r7]]. You send audio and get audio, avatar video and action triggers, without hosting orchestration. It lists over 140 locales for speech to text, over 600 standard voices across 150 or more locales, noise suppression, echo cancellation, phrase lists, custom speech, custom voice and function calling. Models include `gpt-realtime-2.1` (also `-datazone` and `-regional`), `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`, `gpt-realtime-1.5`, `gpt-realtime`, `gpt-realtime-mini`, `gpt-4o` and `gpt-4o-mini`. The agent surface is preview as of 2026-10-13.

**Turn detection** finds when the user started and stopped speaking. A silence timer cannot tell a thinking pause from a finished thought, so semantic types also read the words [[tr3]]. A short silence window feels snappy but cuts in on thinking pauses, and a long one is patient but adds dead air, so tune it against the measured interruption rate.

explain.title: Turn-taking states
explain.alt: The agent listens, the user speaks, an end-of-turn check decides whether the user continues or the agent answers, and a barge-in returns control to the user.
explain.src:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Listening
  Listening --> UserSpeaking: speech detected
  UserSpeaking --> EndCheck: silence
  EndCheck --> UserSpeaking: user continues
  EndCheck --> AgentSpeaking: turn complete
  AgentSpeaking --> UserSpeaking: barge-in
  AgentSpeaking --> Listening: reply done

explain.title: Session setting for a multilingual agent
explain.caption: Field names from the Voice Live how-to. `remove_filler_words` defaults to false and ignores fillers such as 'uh' and 'hmm' while a response plays.

explain.title: Other platforms
explain.md: OpenAI Realtime offers `server_vad` (default) and `semantic_vad` with `eagerness`. Azure OpenAI Realtime accepts `none`, `semantic_vad` or `server_vad` [[r4]] [[r6]].

whereToUse: Contact-centre bots on Azure that need noise suppression and wide locale coverage
Kiosks and in-car assistants with short commands and background noise
Voice tutors where learners pause to think mid-sentence
Multilingual lines where a language-aware end-of-turn check helps

use: Semantic turn detection when callers pause mid-thought, read numbers or switch languages
Tuned `server_vad` for short commands where speed beats patience
`remove_filler_words` when 'uh-huh' keeps cutting the agent off
avoid: Short `silence_duration_ms` with long-winded callers: the agent will talk over them
`semantic_vad` on models other than `gpt-realtime` and `gpt-realtime-mini` in Voice Live
Treating turn detection as only a latency dial
flips: Callers pause to think: raise patience (`eagerness` low or a longer silence window)
Lines are very noisy: retune `threshold` and test semantic types against server VAD
Your model is `gpt-5` or `gpt-4.1`: use the Azure semantic types, not `semantic_vad`

pitfalls.symptom: The agent cuts in when callers pause to think
pitfalls.cause: Silence-based detection cannot tell thinking from finishing
pitfalls.fix: Use a semantic type with patient settings, and measure the interruption rate.

pitfalls.symptom: Backchannels like 'mm-hm' stop the agent mid-sentence
pitfalls.cause: Barge-in fires on any detected speech
pitfalls.fix: Enable `remove_filler_words` and set `languages`. It assumes the client plays audio as it arrives.

pitfalls.symptom: Config is rejected on a chosen model
pitfalls.cause: `semantic_vad` works only with `gpt-realtime` and `gpt-realtime-mini` in Voice Live

scenarios.title: Callers reading account numbers
scenarios.situation: A contact-centre agent on Azure takes digit strings. Callers pause between groups of digits and the agent keeps answering mid-number.
scenarios.question: What do you change?

options.name: Use `azure_semantic_vad` with a longer `silence_duration_ms`
options.why: It reads meaning, works with all models, and a longer window tolerates digit pauses [[tr3]].
options.tradeoff: Slightly slower responses on short replies.

options.name: Switch to `semantic_vad`
options.why: It works only on `gpt-realtime` and `gpt-realtime-mini` in Voice Live, so it is invalid on gpt-4.1.
options.tradeoff: Right if you move to a supported realtime model.

options.name: Raise `threshold` only
options.tradeoff: Does nothing about thinking pauses and can miss quiet callers.

flips.then: Use the multilingual semantic type with `languages` set.

scenarios.takeaway: Pauses mid-utterance call for semantic detection and patience.

scenarios.title: Noisy kiosk commands
scenarios.situation: A public kiosk takes short spoken commands in a loud hall. Users expect an instant reply. Long pauses never occur.
unknowns: Is echo from the kiosk speaker an issue?
scenarios.question: Which turn detection and settings?

options.name: Tuned `server_vad` with a short silence window and tested `threshold`, plus noise suppression and echo cancellation
options.why: Short commands do not need semantic patience, and Voice Live adds noise suppression and echo cancellation [[r7]].
options.tradeoff: Occasional early cut-offs for slow speakers.

options.name: Semantic turn detection with patient settings
options.why: Waiting for meaning adds delay the kiosk does not need.
options.tradeoff: Valuable for conversational flows with pauses.

options.name: Disable turn detection and use push-to-talk
options.tradeoff: Changes the interaction and adds a button.

flips.then: Check echo cancellation and client audio routing first.

scenarios.takeaway: Speed-first command voices can stay on tuned silence detection.

quiz.q: A Voice Live agent on `gpt-4.1` rejects `"type": "semantic_vad"`. What is the right fix?
options: Use `azure_semantic_vad`, which works with all models
quiz.explain: In Voice Live `semantic_vad` is limited to `gpt-realtime` and `gpt-realtime-mini`. The Azure semantic types work with all models. `eagerness` applies only to `semantic_vad`, and the other settings do not change availability.

quiz.q: Which are documented effects of `remove_filler_words` in Voice Live?
options: It ignores fillers such as 'uh' or 'hmm' while a response is in progress
quiz.explain: The option ignores listed English fillers during a response to reduce false barge-in, and is off by default. It has no translation role.

flashcards.front: Which Voice Live turn detection types work with all models?

flashcards.back: How eagerly the model ends the user's turn with `semantic_vad`: `low` waits longer, `high` chunks as soon as possible, `auto` equals `medium`.

flashcards.front: Why can silence-only turn detection misfire?
flashcards.back: It cannot tell a thinking pause from a finished thought, so the agent cuts in. Semantic detection reads the words as well as the audio.
